columns.name: month
columns.label: Month
columns.meaning: The first day of the month in which the incidents happened, taken from the occurrence date. It is the time axis for every trend.

columns.name: AREA NAME
columns.label: Area name
columns.meaning: The name of the area the incident is recorded under in the data file. It is used to compare places across the city.

columns.name: Crm Cd Desc
columns.label: Crime type
columns.meaning: The text description of the crime type recorded for the incident. Some descriptions are cut off in the source file.
columns.example: ASSAULT WITH DEADLY WEAPON, AGGRAVATED ASSAULT

columns.name: incidents
columns.label: Incidents
columns.meaning: The number of reported incidents counted in that row. It is the main measure used in every chart.

columns.name: LAT
columns.label: Latitude
columns.meaning: The middle latitude of all incidents recorded in the area. It places the area on the map.

columns.name: LON
columns.label: Longitude
columns.meaning: The middle longitude of all incidents recorded in the area. It places the area on the map.

columns.name: total_incidents
columns.label: Total incidents
columns.meaning: All incidents counted for the area across every month analyzed. It shows the overall size of the area's caseload.

columns.name: last_12_months
columns.label: Incidents in last 12 months
columns.meaning: Incidents counted in the most recent 12 full months. It is the current period in the comparison.

columns.name: prior_12_months
columns.label: Incidents in prior 12 months
columns.meaning: Incidents counted in the 12 full months before the latest 12. It is the comparison period.

columns.name: change_12m
columns.label: Change over 12 months
columns.meaning: Incidents in the last 12 months minus incidents in the 12 months before. A positive number means a rise.

columns.name: pct_change_12m
columns.label: Percent change over 12 months
columns.meaning: The 12-month change as a percent of the earlier 12 months. It is empty when the earlier period had no incidents.

columns.name: level
columns.label: Series level
columns.meaning: Says whether a row counts the whole city, one area or one crime type. It lets the dashboard filter the long table.

columns.name: name
columns.label: Series name
columns.meaning: The name of the city, area or crime type that the row counts. It goes with the level column.

columns.name: previous_month
columns.label: Incidents in previous month
columns.meaning: The incident count of the same series in the month before. It is empty for the first month.

columns.name: mom_change
columns.label: Change from previous month
columns.meaning: Incidents this month minus incidents last month. A positive number means a rise.

columns.name: mom_pct_change
columns.label: Percent change from previous month
columns.meaning: The month-to-month change as a percent of last month's count. It is empty when last month had no incidents.

columns.name: baseline_mean
columns.label: Usual level
columns.meaning: The average monthly count over the 12 months before this one. It shows what is normal for that series.

columns.name: baseline_std
columns.label: Usual variation
columns.meaning: How much the monthly count normally moves around the usual level, over the prior 12 months. A larger value means a noisier series.

columns.name: z_score
columns.label: Spike score
columns.meaning: How many standard deviations this month sits above its usual level. Higher values mean a more unusual month.

columns.name: flag
columns.label: Spike flag
columns.meaning: Marks months that are far above the usual level by score, size and percent. Other months are marked as within the usual range.

notes: Area names and crime type descriptions come straight from the raw file. Their text was kept as stored.
A month is a calendar month based on the date the incident happened, not the date it was reported.
The area_crime_monthly table only has rows for months with at least one incident, and only for the most common crime types.
